clue.text: Congratulations, having lofted sixes, almost?

parts.note: lofted = high up in the air
numbers that almost reach sixes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is pure cricket — batters lofting sixes — but no letters move at all: 'almost sixes' are simply fives, and the question mark owns up to the arithmetic joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapping raised palms together is a celebratory gesture, so the plural stands for well-done greetings shared after a success.

clue.text: Ferret wounded small creatures in a hole

parts.note: a hob is a male ferret
past tense of bite
standard abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: Tolkien's opening line — 'In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit' — makes the definition fair. HOB for a male ferret is a crossword staple worth filing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's halflings live in burrows dug into hillsides, so the definition describes them by their famous underground dwelling.

clue.text: Try united batter and stew

parts.note: have a go = have a try
as in Man U
to batter = to lash, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'batter' to be the cake mixture next to the stew, but it is the verb — to lash. U for united comes straight off the football results.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hungarian dish of beef and paprika slow-cooked in liquid, it is one specific kind of the general term.

clue.text: Social gathering vital for one usually on laptop

parts.note: a function is a formal social event
key = vital, as in 'a key decision'

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: F1 to F12 run along the top of a laptop keyboard, so a function key is 'one usually on laptop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the F1 to F12 buttons sit along the top row of nearly every laptop keyboard.

clue.text: Selective eaters may have struggles to eat this protein?

parts.note: vies = struggles, competes
the protein that VIES swallows

explanation.walkthrough: Veggies here are the vegetarians, not the vegetables — the selective eaters. The joke is that the wordplay acts out the surface: VIES really does have to eat an EGG.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal shorthand for vegetarians, who avoid meat on principle and so are choosy about what goes on their plates.

clue.text: Had accommodation across river, then wandered off

parts.note: stayed = had accommodation, as at a hotel
map-key abbreviation

explanation.walkthrough: STAYED spans the R just as the surface has the lodgings sitting across the water. R for river is one of the commonest single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stray is to drift away from the right path or from one's group.

clue.text: Tease bird a small distance off

indicators.note: taken off means removed from the bird's name

parts.note: the chaffinch is a common European finch
an inch is a small distance

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a bird that has flown a little way off.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff is to banter with or make fun of someone good-naturedly.

clue.text: Agency's brief goodbye

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so the last letter of the farewell is dropped

parts.note: ciao is the Italian goodbye, used in English too

explanation.surface: A spy agency signs off with a curt farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('Agency is'): the definition is the agency itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The CIA is the American Central Intelligence Agency, the best-known intelligence organisation.

clue.text: Bail due to be reviewed in hearing

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a courtroom, and 'hearing' completes the legal picture so well that it hides the definition: 'in hearing' — within earshot — is AUDIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being within hearing means being loud enough for the ear to pick up, an idiomatic equivalent of the adjective.

clue.text: Having crossed river, shot by arrow in the head, and left like this?

indicators.note: something shot by an arrow has it lodged in it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ford a river is to wade across it, so having done so is forded

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of arrow is used

parts.note: only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A traveller wades a river, takes an arrow to the head and is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase 'left for dead', and the whole scene shows how someone might end up so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left for dead is abandoned in the belief that they will not survive, as an arrow-shot traveller might be.

clue.text: Disaster, going after black bear

parts.note: as in pencil grades
goes after the B

explanation.walkthrough: Bruin — Dutch for brown — is the bear's name in the medieval Reynard fables, and crosswords have kept it alive ever since.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk name for the bear, from the Dutch word for brown used in the medieval Reynard fables.

clue.text: Manipulate voting arrangement, cancelling all-out rally in plant

parts.note: the base word, before surgery
RALLY with ALL out — and this RY is what gets cancelled

explanation.walkthrough: A deletion built from another deletion: the letters to be removed are themselves manufactured by an earlier removal, which is rare and worth slowing down for. Germander is a family of flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing herb of the mint family, genus Teucrium, so it is one particular instance of the general term.

clue.text: Princess on stage may sound like a duck

parts.note: the eider is the sea duck famous for its down

explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta — hence 'on stage'. Say IDA aloud and you get 'eider', the duck whose down fills your duvet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera takes its title from its heroine, a princess met only in the theatre.

clue.text: Unfortunately still barely functioning as an example

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: count the beats in 'func-tion-ing' — three, so the word is itself an example of a trisyllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'functioning' has three beats, func-tion-ing, so it is itself an instance of a three-part word.

clue.text: Despairing, how 'miserable' becomes me

definitions.meaning: to lose heart is to despair
strip the heart — every inner letter — out of MISERABLE and only M…E survives: 'me'

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is an instruction acted out on the word itself: MISERABLE losing its heart leaves just ME. 'Becomes me' adds a layer of false modesty to the gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's courage or hope is to despair; and stripping every inner letter from 'miserable' leaves only its outer pair, spelling 'me'.

clue.text: Academy halved deficit in grand house

parts.note: SCHOOL cut to its first half
a loss = a deficit

explanation.walkthrough: Schloss is the German for a castle or stately home — the grand house. An English academy, halved, opens a German answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from German, the word names a castle or palatial country residence, a stately home in plain terms.

clue.text: Detectives are liable to exaggerate

parts.note: Detective Inspectors
'they tend to' = 'they are liable to'

explanation.walkthrough: To distend is to swell or inflate, and blowing something up beyond its true size is exactly what exaggeration does — that shared image is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or inflate something beyond its natural size is a figurative match for overstating it.

clue.text: More grim to be nearly naked

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: starkers is British slang for stark naked

explanation.surface: Being almost unclothed makes things all the bleaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is jokey British slang for completely naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark means bleak or harsh, so its comparative describes something bleaker and harsher.

clue.text: Spy's simple earring

definitions.meaning: a long-term undercover agent who lies low for years before being activated
a plain ring worn to keep a new piercing open

explanation.walkthrough: Espionage and jewellery, with nothing in common but the word. Railway sleepers would make it a triple — English works this word hard.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a dormant agent planted to await activation; the other is a small plain hoop worn to stop a fresh piercing closing.

clue.text: Way back, wise guy's first to drop a board game

indicators.note: the first letter drops down to the bottom of this downward word, moving to the end

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
Go is the ancient East Asian game of stones on a grid

explanation.surface: Long ago, a clever chap was first to give up on a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'drop' sends the sage's first letter down to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages ago means a very long time in the past, which is what way back means as a time phrase.

clue.text: Turned back, taking opposite directions in circle

parts.note: takes the EW in
east and west, a facing pair on the compass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned back' as a tape or a clock is rewound. Compass points are a setter's favourite way to smuggle in E, W, N and S — 'opposite directions' always means a facing pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding a tape or clock hands toward the start turns them back, so the past tense is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Youngster with Guardian wanting whiskey in pubs shows guts

indicators.note: the stripped youngster sits in the pubs, so it goes inside them

parts.note: inns are pubs

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a ward is a young person placed under a guardian's care
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newspaper-reading youngster turns down whiskey in pubs and shows some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian is the newspaper on the surface but a legal guardian in the wordplay; 'shows' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Innards are the internal organs, especially the stomach and intestines, that is the guts.

clue.text: Happening before delivery to change routine

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is the midwife's, not the postman's: in utero means in the womb, so before delivery. A neat single-word anagram — ROUTINE rearranged completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'in the womb', describing anything that occurs before a baby is born.

clue.text: Run a brief fiddle making pasta

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the instrument's last letter goes

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Someone runs a quick scam that ends up producing pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle suggests a swindle, but here it is the instrument; R is the cricket abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square parcels of filled pasta, an example of the Italian food.

clue.text: A way to heave and strain

parts.note: a street
to retch is to heave, in the queasy sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' defines STRETCH as verb or noun. The surface implies hauling on a rope, but the heaving here is the stomach's — to retch.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a muscle or rope taut is to strain it, a plain synonym that works as verb or noun.

clue.text: Bizarrely we envy almost all that's horrible in author

parts.note: anagram fodder
ALL stopping short of its last letter
the exclamation of disgust joins the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh wrote Decline and Fall and Brideshead Revisited, and the surface reads like a review of his satire: we do envy almost all that's horrible in him.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist behind Brideshead Revisited and Scoop, so the definition names him by his profession.

clue.text: One checks whistleblower in French department

definitions.meaning: the Video Assistant Referee reviews the on-pitch referee's decisions
one of the French departments along the Mediterranean coast in Provence, named after the river running through it

explanation.walkthrough: The whistleblower is not a leaker but the referee holding an actual whistle, second-guessed from the VAR booth every football weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Football's video assistant referee reviews decisions by the official on the pitch, and the same three letters name a Provence département after its river.

clue.text: Wendy's theatre?

definitions.meaning: a child's toy Wendy house, named for Wendy in Peter Pan, is a miniature den for pretend games
loads of real theatres use this exact word as their proper name

explanation.walkthrough: The Lost Boys build a little house around Wendy in Peter Pan, which is how toy houses got the name — and since Peter Pan began as a play, the question mark is well earned.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a child's toy den for make-believe, and many theatres carry this word in their proper names.

clue.text: Partner dropping by in centre of activity

parts.note: an informal husband
the letters dropped from HUBBY

explanation.walkthrough: The letters to remove are sitting right there in the clue: hubby drops 'by', and the deletion hides in plain sight as the visitor 'dropping by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The central part of a wheel lends its name figuratively to any focal point where things happen.

clue.text: Under way a short distance

definitions.meaning: an old idiom for something already under way, as in a famous detective's saying
twelve inches make a common unit of length; stick the indefinite article in front of it to build the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer and 'a foot' really is a short distance. 'The game's afoot' was Shakespeare's line in Henry V long before Sherlock Holmes borrowed it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something in progress or brewing; split in two it is also the indefinite article plus a twelve-inch measure.

clue.text: Foreign character doctor found in shape

parts.note: the Greek letter
Bachelor of Medicine, from the Latin Medicinae Baccalaureus

explanation.walkthrough: A rhomb is a rhombus with its Latin tail docked. Crossword doctors come in many flavours — DR, MO, GP and, as here, MB.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant name for the diamond-shaped quadrilateral with four equal sides, so it is one specific geometric figure.

clue.text: Opposite of gauche, that missing husband in spa town

parts.note: French: gauche is left, droit is right
the pronoun
the abbreviation removed from WHICH

explanation.walkthrough: Droitwich Spa in Worcestershire made its name on salt and brine baths. Droit, the French for right, also gives English 'adroit' — the opposite of gauche in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Worcestershire town famed for its brine baths and officially styled with 'Spa' after its name, so it fits the description.
